findings.title: Created CID is lost at create cancellation or contradictory private stderr, so cleanup skips the owned container
findings.requirement: Register and retain every possibly-created owned CID; Docker CLI termination is not daemon settlement. Do not abandon a created stopped container when acquisition acknowledgment fails.
findings.mechanism: docker() validates exit/stderr before returning create stdout. The caller assigns and checkpoints cid only after that return and regex validation. Its finally cleanup is guarded by h03 and cid. The private --cidfile is never read. Thus a successful create with stderr or cancellation after daemon creation leaves cid empty and skips exact resource cleanup.
findings.observed: Both cases retain the private CID file and a seam-created container, but cid_checkpointed=false and daemon_removed_seam=false. Cancellation kills/joins only the substituted direct CLI. The DB fence remains set, which is correct, but the container locator/cleanup is lost. The positive normal case checkpoints and removes the exact CID.
findings.remedy: Register provisional nonce/name/cidfile ownership before create; recover and strictly attest the exact CID before raising validation/cancellation failures. Preserve uncertainty on missing/lost acknowledgments, retain recovery locators, and clean an attested stopped container without relying on a Host socket. Do not clear unknown daemon state merely after killing the CLI.
findings.limit: Actual unmodified SOURCE helper and create/finally call-site AST; daemon/CLI seams are explicitly substituted. No physical Docker timeout/cancellation was executed.

findings.title: Known created-but-unstarted containers cannot be cleaned because retirement first requires a live Host RPC connection
findings.requirement: Own cleanup for all acquisition phases, including static containment refusal and pre-boot/start failure; attempt exact stopped-container cleanup independently of native readiness.
findings.mechanism: retire_host() always connects and drains before issuing Docker stop or rm. An acquired CID with no runtime.boot/runtime.sock cannot satisfy that connection. The cleanup raises before any Docker retirement/removal, despite having the exact created CID.
findings.observed: After create and inspect, an injected pre-boot start failure leaves runtime.writer=None. Actual cleanup calls connect and raises; no stop/rm follows, the known container remains, and DB uncertainty is retained. The normal control reaches exact rm and absence readback.
findings.remedy: Separate attested resource-state cleanup from graceful native drain. For a known never-started/stopped owned container, verify identity/state and remove only that exact CID without Host RPC. For an uncertain/running phase, attempt all bounded owned cleanup and preserve unknown outcomes plus locators rather than abandoning subsequent resource steps.
findings.limit: SOURCE consumer lifecycle with substituted finite Host and daemon seams; no native or container launched.

findings.title: Pre-boot containment oracle accepts undeclared mounts, host PID namespace, privileged state and environment; daemon identity is not bound
findings.requirement: Attest the full actual created-container configuration, daemon identity and exact owned mounts before boot; prohibit Docker socket and personal-profile mounts and require private PID namespace/confinement.
findings.mechanism: The created-container check reads only selected Config/HostConfig fields. It ignores top-level Mounts, Config.Env/Volumes, HostConfig.PidMode/Privileged and resource limits/tmpfs. No daemon identity receipt is acquired or compared across calls. h03_container_argv checks lexical absolute paths, not physical owned roots, and accepts a scratch symlink resolving outside scratch.
findings.observed: The actual pre-start if-node rejects the network-mode negative but accepts every other named mutation, including an extra Docker socket or personal-profile mount. The actual argv builder accepts an owned scratch symlink resolving to /home/kali/.hermes. Only symlink metadata was inspected, no credential files. Static image readback independently confirms immutable ID, stock Cmd, null Entrypoint, UID1000:1000 and no image-declared Volumes; that valid image does not supply the missing actual-container/daemon checks.
findings.remedy: Before first start, bind read-only daemon identity, compare the complete relevant create configuration to the exact plan and validate the complete canonical mount inventory (sources, destinations, types, RW/options/propagation). Require physical owned non-symlink roots and private PID mode; compare environment, privilege, limits/tmpfs and reject undeclared mounts/configuration. Repeat identity readback where subsequent effects depend on it. Reuse existing attestation logic, not a third framework.
findings.limit: These are false-green attestation controls on unmodified SOURCE, not evidence that Docker itself currently added unauthorized mounts or that the installed image is compromised. The current caller creates fresh direct directories; the path negative demonstrates the helper's input boundary.

findings.title: DB destruction fence is released after later apparent Docker cleanup despite prior unknown daemon work, and before public owner cleanup
findings.requirement: Unknown lifecycle outcomes remain latched; the dynamic DB fence must outlive every owned effect/family/public-owner cleanup. A later exact-CID absence is not proof that an earlier effectful Docker request settled.
findings.mechanism: docker() kills/joins the direct CLI on cancellation but has no persistent effect-uncertainty latch. Cleanup later assigns db_fence.unsettled=false solely after successful retirement/rm/absence. That assignment also occurs before runtime.close(), public_control.__aexit__ and engine disposal. Failures of those later cleanup steps cannot restore the fence.
findings.observed: The actual retire_host first reaches stop, the substituted communicate producer cancels while daemon work remains in flight, and the direct CLI is killed/joined. A later normal cleanup retry emits the settled claim and clears the fence with daemon_inflight_seam=true. Separately, the complete unmodified run-finally AST reaches an injected public-owner exit failure after exact-CID removal; engine disposal executes, but db_retained=false and the settled resource claim already exists. The normal control clears the fence only with no injected unknown/failure.
findings.remedy: Latch uncertainty before every effectful Docker/reader child launch and preserve it for cancellation, timeout, unknown exit or lost acknowledgment until the existing authoritative settlement mechanism resolves that exact request/family. Do not equate a retry or current absence with original request settlement. Move fence release after all resource, runtime, public-control, child-family and engine cleanup readbacks, retaining it on any failure. Reuse H01's existing strict family authority where applicable; do not build a new supervisor.
findings.limit: Unmodified SOURCE producer/helper and full finally with substituted daemon/Host/public-owner seams. This proves unsafe fence transitions, not physical daemon settlement. Actual H03 child timeout-family behavior remains unexecuted under this review authority.
